tasks.short: Prepare geography syllabi, assignments and handouts with verified sources and human academic checking.

steps.what: Set course outcomes, assignment purposes and the syllabus sequence
Retrieve verified readings, geographic examples and existing course materials
Prepare syllabi, homework assignments and handout explanations from the selected sources

loop.purpose: Draft course text and assignment prompts from teacher-selected content
loop.input: Outcomes, level, calendar and verified geographic sources
loop.output: Draft syllabus, prompts and explanations with source references
loop.check: Teacher checks learning alignment, geographic meaning, dates and whether assignments can be answered from the supplied sources
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported examples or unsuitable tasks require manual preparation
loop.why_not_simpler: Native layouts provide headings but not the topic-specific explanation or assignment wording

steps.what: Arrange the handout layout, map captions and assignment fields
Check academic accuracy, map interpretation, assignment feasibility and syllabus dates
Save the final prepared materials in the existing course document workspace

tasks.design: Use outcomes from {LMS}, source references from {OTHER}, the reference manager, and native material layouts in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting step prepares text; layout work, academic checking and the ordinary same-system save remain separate, with the save fully retained and ungated.
tasks.previous_blocker: First-draft wording and repeated course-document layout take time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and source-grounded drafting can reuse verified geography examples.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching alignment, accurate map interpretation and suitable assignments.
tasks.human_edge: Subject judgement about what students should understand and how to assess it.
tasks.altitude: Spend preparation attention on teaching value rather than repeated wording and layout.

reach.task: Trace assignment purpose to learning outcomes

evidence.claim: Scopus AI supplies topic summaries and foundational papers, supporting source discovery rather than automatic validation of course content.
Reviewed course drafting and native layouts may reduce preparation effort; the benefit is E1.

assumptions: This task owns syllabi, homework and handouts. Lecture-specific speaking narrative and delivery belong to task 6006 and are not counted again.
The teacher supplies outcomes, level and calendar in s1, verifies source identifiers and examples in s2 and captures required fields during s3-s4. Missing dates or sources require manual preparation.
Native material templates are tried before the drafting loop. Existing maps are used; no automatic map production or publication is implied.
The ordinary author save in s6 is small, fully retained and requires no self-approval. This task prepares materials without inventing a distribution action.
unknowns: Reusability of existing layouts and teaching examples
research_questions: Does reviewed drafting reduce total material preparation after checking geographic meaning and assignment feasibility?

already_counted.description: Draft review and full academic checking

incremental.description: Maintain material templates and source-grounded drafting checks

tasks.short: Prepare lecture-specific explanations and teach geography through checked examples and responsive discussion.

steps.what: Select the lecture's teaching argument and difficult geographic concepts to explain
Retrieve current urbanization, environmental systems or cultural geography examples
Write lecture explanations, transitions and questions for the selected topic

loop.input: Teacher-selected argument, verified examples and student level
loop.output: Draft speaking narrative and questions linked to examples
loop.check: Teacher checks geographic interpretation, level and the reasoning expressed by each example
loop.stop: One revision; misleading examples or unsupported explanations return to manual preparation
loop.why_not_simpler: Reusable slide layouts do not express the selected lecture argument

steps.what: Check and revise the lecture's claims, figures and teaching sequence
Check and deliver lectures and answer undergraduate or graduate student questions
Record explanations to revisit and useful post-lecture teaching adjustments

tasks.design: Link verified examples from {OTHER}, the reference manager, to lecture-specific writing in {DOCS}. A bounded draft supports the speaking narrative, while academic revision, live delivery and the later teaching note are separate human steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lecture-specific explanations and example navigation add preparation effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-linked drafting and native teaching-note layouts can reuse verified material.
tasks.still_hard: Making spatial and cultural relationships understandable and answering unexpected questions.
tasks.human_edge: Responsive explanation and reading students' understanding.
tasks.altitude: Spend more attention on geographic explanation and responsive teaching.

evidence.claim: Source-linked lecture drafting and reusable teaching-note layouts are plausible E1 capabilities; the digest has no measured geography lecture result.

assumptions: Course handouts and syllabus production belong to task 6011. This task includes lecture-specific writing, revision, delivery and its actual working follow-up note.
The teacher supplies the argument in s1, verifies example dates and meaning in s2 and captures teaching adjustments in s6. Missing or incompatible examples require manual preparation.
Native reusable examples and layouts precede the model loop. No automatic source collection or LMS publication is implied.
Ordinary internal author saves remain fully retained without self-approval.
unknowns: How much lecture wording is actually written today
Currency and compatibility of geographic examples
research_questions: Does drafted speaking narrative reduce total preparation effort after checking each geographic explanation?

already_counted.description: Draft review and full lecture revision

incremental.description: Maintain lecture source links and drafting checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact final lecture claims, figures and intended student audience checked before delivery; changed examples or claims require another check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R86 gives14 gross minus3 upkeep =11 net. Low: dated examples need replacement and explanations are largely rewritten, leaving retrieval14, writing23 and notes4 plus55 unchanged, R96; net1. High: source examples fit but substantial speaking adaptation remains, leaving13+18+4+55=90 retained; net7 after3 upkeep. Topic choice, revision and delivery stay full.

tasks.short: Conduct geography research, record evidence, write findings and separately publish the checked manuscript.

steps.what: Define the geography research question and study method
Retrieve verified literature, geographic datasets and source references
Conduct fieldwork, interviews or documentary study according to the research method
Record research observations, spatial metadata and source references
Analyse the evidence and interpret spatial relationships and limitations
Write the findings manuscript and its source-linked explanation

loop.purpose: Draft findings prose from the researcher's interpretation
loop.input: Study method, interpreted findings and verified references
loop.output: Draft manuscript sections with explicit limitations and sources
loop.check: Researcher verifies every empirical claim and causal or spatial interpretation against the evidence
loop.stop: One revision pass; unsupported claims or confidential evidence require manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: A manuscript template cannot express the study-specific argument

steps.what: Check and revise the manuscript's findings, references and publication claims
Check the final manuscript package and submit it to the publication venue

tasks.design: Use native source and research-record views in {OTHER}, the bibliographic and geographic research software, with manuscript writing in {DOCS}. Source retrieval, observation capture and bounded prose drafting may become quicker; study conduct, analysis, final checking and the publication submission through {PARTNER_PORTAL} remain separate human work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated source and observation metadata and first manuscript prose add handling around original research.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record forms and source-linked drafts can reuse researcher-supplied evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Sound methods, spatial inference and a defensible research contribution.
tasks.human_edge: Original scientific judgement and responsibility for the published claim.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated evidence and prose handling while retaining research judgement.

reach.task: Maintain a traceable study evidence pack

evidence.claim: Scopus AI provides topic summaries and foundational papers, supporting literature discovery rather than research inference.
Native evidence forms and reviewed manuscript drafting may reduce handling; the proposed benefit is E1.

assumptions: The baseline includes original research, actual evidence capture, manuscript writing and publication submission.

The researcher supplies method in s1, verifies source identities in s2 and records observation identity, date, source and applicable spatial reference metadata in s4 from s3. Capture is counted; missing or incompatible coordinates remain manual exceptions.
S6 consumes only interpreted findings created in s5 and verified sources. No automated inference, map generation or dataset transfer is implied.
Native templates precede the loop. Existing analytical software runtime and ordinary author saves receive no new saving or approval stage.
unknowns: Research method and spatial metadata compatibility
Actual manuscript and observation entry effort
research_questions: Does reviewed drafting save total manuscript effort after source, spatial inference and limitation checking?

already_counted.description: Manuscript draft review and full final claim checking

incremental.description: Maintain study form mappings and source-grounded writing checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact final manuscript, evidence attachments, author information and publication venue checked before submission; any change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 B100 R88 gives12 gross minus4 upkeep =8 net. Low: datasets use incompatible spatial metadata and the draft's interpretation needs rewriting, leaving retrieval10, capture9 and writing17 plus60 unchanged, R96; net0. High: stable source identifiers reduce handling while substantive prose edits remain, leaving9+8+14+60=91 retained; net5 after4 upkeep. Research conduct, analysis and final publication checking stay full.

tasks.short: Assess geography assignments, determine grades and separately write and release checked feedback.

steps.what: Retrieve students' class work, assignments, papers and the marking rubric
Evaluate students' geographic reasoning, source use and map or data interpretations
Determine grades and resolve ambiguous or exceptional assignment evidence
Write explanatory feedback on the student's reasoning and improvement priorities

loop.purpose: Draft feedback from the teacher's assessment notes
loop.input: Passage-linked observations, rubric and already determined grade
loop.output: Draft feedback preserving the teacher's judgement
loop.check: Teacher verifies each comment against the student's actual geographic argument and removes invented errors or praise
loop.stop: One revision; unsupported comments or misleading map interpretation require manual feedback
loop.why_not_simpler: A native comment bank is tried first but cannot express every assignment-specific explanation

steps.what: Enter the determined grades and reviewed feedback in the unpublished gradebook
Check final student mappings and release the grades and feedback to students

tasks.design: Configure assignment and rubric views in {LMS}, with a bounded draft of feedback from the teacher's own notes. Academic evaluation and grade decisions remain human; unpublished grade entry and the actual release to students are separate actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated work navigation, feedback phrasing and result mapping add marking effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Instructor-note-based feedback drafting is an existing capability, combined with native rubric views.
tasks.still_hard: Judging geographic reasoning and explaining a defensible grade.
tasks.human_edge: Accountable subject judgement about the student's actual work.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated feedback wording while retaining examiner responsibility.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes.
The supplied feedback studies do not establish this geography marking labour benefit; the estimate is E1.

assumptions: The teacher is the authorised examiner. No model evaluates learning outcomes or determines grades in this design.

The LMS supplies submission and student identity in s1; the teacher produces passage-linked assessment notes in s2 and grades in s3. Capture time is counted, and missing mappings are reconciled manually.
Native rubrics and reusable comments precede the loop. No second-system transfer is assumed from the digest's one institutional example.
The ordinary author save in the unpublished gradebook is fully retained and ungated; only release to students requires a final-version gate.
unknowns: Actual share of bespoke map and data feedback
research_questions: Does reviewed feedback drafting reduce total marking effort while preserving grades and the meaning of geographic explanations?

already_counted.description: Full grade determination and feedback draft review

incremental.description: Maintain rubric prompts and sample feedback quality

approvals.approved_version: Exact final student identifiers, grades, feedback and release audience checked before publication; changes require another check.

Low: map feedback needs bespoke wording and sparse notes force substantial rewriting, leaving retrieval9, feedback23 and entry9 plus55 unchanged, R96; net0. High: passage-linked notes fit the rubric but spatial explanations need edits, leaving9+18+8+55=90 retained; net6 after4 upkeep. Reading, grade judgement and actual release stay full.

reach: Prepare source-traceable course and research packs
